newsitem.title: KUWAIT: ILO urges Kuwait to introduce minimum wage.
newsitem.headline: ILO urges Kuwait to introduce minimum wage.

text.p: The International Labour Organisation has urged Kuwait to introduce a minimum wage and place domestic help under the umbrella of a pending labour law, an ILO official was quoted on Thursday as saying.

The head of the ILO's Kuwait office, Abubakr Badawi, also told Arab Times in an interview "We hope the new labour code would cover the area of equity between males and females...We look for more relaxation in the area of forming trade unions."
Some 700,000 of Kuwait's two million population are citizens while the rest are expatriate workers and their families, and stateless Arabs.

Badawi said the ILO was prepared to "help the government adopt viable and practical alternatives for the sponsor system" for foreign workers which is also implemented in other Gulf Arab states. He said the current system had "a lot of weaknesses".
The majority of foreign workers in Kuwait must have a Kuwaiti sponsor to acquire a residency and other permits.

Badawi's remarks included a call for a pension and retirement scheme for expatriate workers in Kuwait. "There should be no difference between national and foreign labour with regards to social security," he told the English-language daily.

He said the government had earlier asked an ILO expert to study the proposed Labour Law "to see how much this draft is taking into consideration the international labour standards. We do not interfere in the process of drafting or ratifying the labour code," he added.
